A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evolving multi-agent curriculum research, with the original self-paced procedure identifiable in v2. Text, equations, figures, tables, and v1 Appendices A–C are readable. V2 ends with references and contains no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original Pursuit, Simple-Spread, and Simple-Push experiments, including architecture comparisons and training curves in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments on sparse-reward Simple-Spread, a 10-player XOR game, and SMACv2 Protoss 5 vs. 5.

M1.justification: V1's SPMARL updates curricula using initial-state values. V2 retains this procedure as SPRL and introduces critic-loss learning-progress maximization for the first stage (Equations 8–9 and Algorithm 1), while retaining the return threshold and target-distribution stage. The instantiated learner also changes from IPPO to MAPPO with a centralized critic.

E1.justification: Pursuit and cooperative Simple-Push are removed, while the 10-player XOR game and SMACv2 Protoss 5 vs. 5 are added. Simple-Spread remains but is evaluated with a newly specified sparse reward. This substantially changes the evaluated tasks and domains.

E2.justification: V1 compares against IPPO, linear curricula, and, in Pursuit, EPC and VACL with uniform/Gaussian targets; Appendix B also evaluates AttIPPO. V2 instead evaluates MAPPO without a teacher, Linear, Random, and reward-based SPRL. The latter corresponds to v1's proposed procedure; EPC, VACL, and AttIPPO comparisons disappear.

E3.justification: Simple-Spread retains an eight-agent/eight-landmark target, but replaces distance penalties with landmark-coverage rewards available only when at least four landmarks are covered, and switches training from IPPO to MAPPO. New SMAC experiments use terminal rewards of +1/−1 and test win rate. These changes prevent direct comparison of performance across versions.

E4.justification: V1's agent-count-only/grid-size-only ablations, sum-versus-average reward study, and fully connected-versus-attention comparison are removed. V2 instead tests critic-loss prioritization against reward-based SPRL and examines the resulting curriculum and training trajectories. The substantive questions investigated change considerably.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3 specifies five algorithmic runs with standard-deviation shading. V2 Figure 3 specifies five random seeds with 95% confidence intervals. The uncertainty convention changes, while the stated repetition count remains five; this does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V1's Pursuit gains and similar final performance across methods on its MPE tasks are replaced. V2 Figure 3 reports failure of Linear and MAPPO without a teacher on sparse Simple-Spread; Figure 5 shows both self-paced methods reaching the XOR optimum before Linear. Figure 7 reports comparable final SMAC performance for SPMARL and SPRL, with faster SPMARL convergence. These are results under changed conditions.

T1.justification: V2 adds the formal definition of learning progress as expected squared return–value error and its importance-weighted optimization objective (Equations 8–9). The existing SPRL constrained formulation is retained, alongside expanded standard MAPPO/GAE mathematics. This is a limited formal addition, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes principled control of agent count and environmental factors, including when agent-count curricula help and how reward aggregation matters. V2 centers its contributions on identifying shortcomings of reward-based curricula and addressing them through critic-loss prioritization, claiming faster convergence on challenging sparse-reward tasks.

C2.justification: V1 discusses reward averaging, collisions, transfer between contexts, and cases where agent-count curricula provide little benefit. V2 replaces these interpretations with arguments about uninformative high-return tasks, credit assignment, and critic loss providing denser and more stable signals. It also newly questions whether the KL constraint remains necessary.

D1.justification: V1 Appendix A supplies learner and curriculum hyperparameter tables plus hardware and runtime estimates. V2 removes these without comparable MAPPO specifications, but adds observation-padding guidance, environment-wrapper information, threshold-selection advice, and a code-access link in Section 4.3. The linked material's contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around critic-loss learning progress versus reward-based curricula, adding discussion of teacher–student curricula, CURIOUS, reward-guided curricula, and PORTAL. It removes much of v1's independent-learning and architecture positioning, including the extended critique of VACL's target distribution.

P1.justification: The title changes from Self-Paced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning to Learning Progress Driven Multi-Agent Curriculum. The abstract, introduction, discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten; related work moves before background, and the method section is reorganized around SPRL, the new SPMARL objective, and implementation factors.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the earlier experimental displays with consistently arranged three-panel benchmark plots using new axes, legends, and styling. It adds a teacher–student optimization diagram, XOR payoff matrix, and SMAC screenshot, replaces the introductory task illustration, and removes the appendix tables and plots. The document also adopts a wider text layout.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a substantive method extension and direct comparisons supporting faster convergence on sparse Simple-Spread and SMACv2. However, standalone reproducibility weakens through removal of detailed training specifications, and the claimed credit-assignment mechanism is not directly tested. Section 5.3 also inconsistently mentions an eight-agent target while Figure 7 specifies five. These gains and documentation/evidence weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain; the PDFs cannot establish whether the linked code resolves the missing details.
